panels.subtitle: Rigveda 10.125 | Vagambhrini Sukta | Spoken by Vak
panels.prose_html:
The Goddess speaks. This hymn is voiced by Vak — Speech — daughter of the seer Ambhrina. Every verse begins with aham, “I”: She carries the Gods, feeds the one who offers, makes seers and sages, draws the bow for Rudra, gives birth to the Father, and reaches beyond Sky and Earth.

It stands in the tenth mandala of the Rigveda, among the cosmological hymns, and is one of the few Vedic hymns spoken wholly in a goddess's own voice. The Shakta tradition reads it as the earliest scriptural statement of the Goddess as supreme power; it is recited at the close of the Devi Mahatmya.

Seer: Vak Ambhrini · Deity: Vak · Metre: Trishtubh (verse 2 is Jagati)

panels.title: Devi Sukta in English
panels.subtitle: Rigveda 10.125 | Translation
panels.prose_html:
1. I move with the Rudras and the Vasus, I with the Adityas and all the Gods; I bear both Mitra and Varuna, I bear Indra and Agni, I both Ashvins.

2. I bear the swelling Soma, I bear Tvashtar, Pushan and Bhaga; I bestow wealth on the one who offers, on the devout patron who presses the Soma.

3. I am the Queen, gatherer of treasures, the knowing one, first among those worthy of worship; the Gods set Me in many places, abiding in many, entering into many.

4. Through Me eats whoever eats, whoever sees, whoever breathes, whoever hears what is spoken; not knowing Me, they still dwell in Me. Hear, O' one who hears: what I tell you is worthy of faith.

5. I Myself proclaim this, welcomed by Gods and by humans; whomever I love, that one I make mighty, a Brahman, a seer, a sage.

6. I stretch the bow for Rudra, so the arrow strikes the hater of prayer; I make battle for the people, I have entered Sky and Earth.

7. I give birth to the Father at the summit of this world; My womb is within the Waters, in the ocean; from there I spread through all beings, and touch that Sky with My height.

8. I Myself blow forth like the Wind, taking hold of all beings; beyond the Sky, beyond this Earth, so great have I become by My greatness.
